title: Simultaneous strict coefficient comparisons on ring-sheaf towers
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism on small sites, with left-exact inverse image $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$. For $W=X,Y$ and $a=0,1,2$, let $R^a_{W,\bullet}$ be inverse sequences of commutative ring sheaves, with maps $i^{ab}_W:R^a_{W,\bullet}\to R^b_{W,\bullet}$ for $a\le b$, $i^{aa}=1$, $i^{02}=i^{12}i^{01}$. Let $\phi^a:u^{-1}R^a_{Y,\bullet}\to R^a_{X,\bullet}$ commute with all coefficient and sequence maps. A strict cochain system consists of possibly unbounded complexes of module sheaves with semilinear chain transitions; its morphisms commute with every transition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Use the actual sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $F_aK=R^a_{X,\bullet}\otimes_{u^{-1}R^a_{Y,\bullet}}u^{-1}K$ and $S^{ab}_WK=R^b_{W,\bullet}\otimes_{R^a_{W,\bullet}}K$, termwise, and let $T_a$ be signed direct-sum total tensor. For fixed coefficients, $c_a:F_aT_a\cong T_a(F_a,F_a)$ is the normalized comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

There are unique simultaneous natural chain isomorphisms $\kappa^{ab}:S_X^{ab}F_a\cong F_bS_Y^{ab}$ and $\sigma_W^{ab}:S_W^{ab}T_a\cong T_b(S_W^{ab},S_W^{ab})$ with the following local formulas in every sequence level and homogeneous bidegree (inverse-image notation on sections is suppressed):
$$\kappa^{ab}:b\otimes(a\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x),\qquad
(\kappa^{ab})^{-1}:b\otimes(d\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,\phi^b(d)\otimes(1\otimes x),$$
$$\sigma_W^{ab}:b\otimes(x\otimes y)\longmapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y),\qquad
(\sigma_W^{ab})^{-1}:(b\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)\longmapsto bd\otimes(x\otimes y).$$
Here $a$ is an $R^a_X$ coefficient and $d$ in the inverse formula for $\kappa$ is a section of $u^{-1}R^b_Y$; all formulas denote generalized local tensor generators after sheafification. Together with $c_a$, these maps and their inverses are maps of strict systems, preserving both differential summands $dx\otimes y$ and $(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ for $x\in K^p$. They satisfy
$$c_b\,F_b(\sigma_Y^{ab})\,\kappa^{ab}_{T_a(K,H)}
=T_b(\kappa_K^{ab},\kappa_H^{ab})\,\sigma_X^{ab}\,S_X^{ab}(c_a).$$
Both composites send $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. This is equality of chain maps and hence of their inverse chain maps, retaining every sequence transition.

Let $U_W^a:S_W^{aa}\cong1$ be $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$ and $A_W:S_W^{12}S_W^{01}\cong S_W^{02}$ be $d\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto d\,i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x$. Under $U$, $\kappa^{aa}$ and $\sigma^{aa}$ are identities. Under $A$, the composite $S_X^{12}S_X^{01}F_0\to S_X^{12}F_1S_Y^{01}\to F_2S_Y^{12}S_Y^{01}$ equals $\kappa^{02}$, and the composite $S_W^{12}S_W^{01}T_0\to S_W^{12}T_1(S_W^{01},S_W^{01})\to T_2(S_W^{12}S_W^{01},S_W^{12}S_W^{01})$ equals $\sigma_W^{02}$. In the latter equality both routes on $d\otimes(b\otimes(x\otimes y))$ have value $(d\,i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. The unit, composition, and square equations hold in strict systems, in both directions. No boundedness, flatness, normalization, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent extraction of old scalar-extension-tower-coherence proof steps 3--7; Stacks Tag 03EL, sites-modules.tex, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Tag 07A4, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-tensor-product. The simultaneous strict-system and coefficient-composition assertions are agent calculations extending these constituents.

proof.text: Work at a fixed sequence level, suppressing its index. Apply [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] to the ringed morphism with coefficient map $\phi^a$ to obtain $c_a$. Apply it also to the identity geometric morphism on $W$, equipped with $i_W^{ab}$; its pullback is exactly $S_W^{ab}$, so its normalized tensor comparison is $\sigma_W^{ab}$ with the two formulas in the statement. To obtain $\kappa$ as an isomorphism, use that lemma's canonical pullback-composition isomorphism. The ringed morphism with geometric part $u$ and coefficient map $u^{-1}R_Y^a\to R_X^b$ has two factorizations: first $F_a$ then $S_X^{ab}$, or first $S_Y^{ab}$ then $F_b$. Their coefficient maps agree by $i_X^{ab}\phi^a=\phi^b u^{-1}i_Y^{ab}$. Each composition comparison identifies its iterated pullback with this single pullback. Composing one comparison with the inverse of the other gives $\kappa^{ab}:S_X^{ab}F_a\cong F_bS_Y^{ab}$. These are actual natural chain isomorphisms; Step 2 expands their scalar-association normalization.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: Spell out the scalar association in Step 1. For $r\in u^{-1}R_Y^a$, balancing $a\phi^a(r)\otimes x=a\otimes rx$ in the source of $\kappa$ gives the same image, since $i_X^{ab}\phi^a(r)=\phi^b i_Y^{ab}(r)$ and the latter scalar can move into $1\otimes rx$. Balancing its outer tensor over $R_X^a$ is multiplication by $i_X^{ab}(a)$. For its proposed inverse, balancing $d i_Y^{ab}(r)\otimes x=d\otimes rx$ has the same image by that same square, and balancing the outer tensor over $u^{-1}R_Y^b$ multiplies by $\phi^b(d)$. These give precisely the two displayed formulas. Composing them sends $b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ to $b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x)=b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ and $b\otimes(d\otimes x)$ to $b\phi^b(d)\otimes(1\otimes x)=b\otimes(d\otimes x)$. Additivity and balancing determine the sectionwise tensor maps; the unique factorization through sheafification extends these equalities to sheaf maps. This argument uses generalized inverse-image generators via the already constructed comparison of Step 1, and does not assume that arbitrary inverse-image sections come from sections on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: For $\sigma$, moving a coefficient $r\in R_W^a$ from $x$ to $y$ changes $(b\otimes rx)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes ry)$ by balancing over $R_W^b$. Its proposed inverse is balanced over $R_W^b$ because $b e d=bd e$, and over $R_W^a$ by the original tensor relation. The two composites reduce respectively to $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ and $(bd\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)=(b\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)$. Thus the normalization from Step 1 has exactly the inverse claimed. Every equality is additive on tensor generators and extends uniquely through the sheafifications in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This same universal property, degree by degree, proves uniqueness of both normalized families. Naturality sends $x,y$ to their images under the given module maps in these formulas, so the two orders agree.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: All four generator formulas leave cochain degrees unchanged and use only degree-zero coefficient multiplication. For example $\sigma$ sends the first differential term $b\otimes(dx\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes dx)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, and the second term $(-1)^p b\otimes(x\otimes dy)$ to $(-1)^p(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes dy)$. The inverse multiplies $b,d$ without changing either sign. For $\kappa$ the equality with the differential is $b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes dx)$ on both sides, and for its inverse it is $b\phi^b(d)\otimes(1\otimes dx)$. The fixed $c_a$ has these properties by [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. That lemma, including its identity-geometric-morphism specialization, already supplies comparisons on the direct-sum total complexes, so no interchange with an infinite product is used. Equality on each summand implies equality on the direct sum by its defining universal property.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: Let $\rho_W^a:R^a_{W,m}\to R^a_{W,n}$ be any sequence transition, and let $t_K$ be its semilinear chain transition. The induced transition on a scalar extension sends $b\otimes x$ to $\rho_W^b(b)\otimes t_Kx$. For $\kappa$ the two orders applied to $b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ give $\rho_X^b(b) i_{X,n}^{ab}(\rho_X^a(a))\otimes(1\otimes t_Kx)$, using $\rho_X^b i_{X,m}^{ab}=i_{X,n}^{ab}\rho_X^a$. For its inverse the two orders give $\rho_X^b(b)\phi_n^b(u^{-1}\rho_Y^b(d))\otimes(1\otimes t_Kx)$ by the assumed transition square for $\phi$. For $\sigma$ both orders give $(\rho_W^b(b)\otimes t_Kx)\otimes(1\otimes t_Hy)$, and for its inverse they give $\rho_W^b(b)\rho_W^b(d)\otimes(t_Kx\otimes t_Hy)$. The analogous formula for $c_a$ is $(\rho_X^a(a)\otimes t_Kx)\otimes(1\otimes t_Hy)$. The generator and sheafification uniqueness from Steps 2–3 proves all these equalities as sheaf maps. These are arbitrary semilinear transitions, not only quotient-unit transitions. Hence the levelwise isomorphisms and their inverses are strict-system morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: To verify the coefficient/tensor square, retain all scalar generators. On $b\otimes(a\otimes(x\otimes y))$ its left route first gives $b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes(x\otimes y))$, then $b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes((1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y))$, and finally $(b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x))\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes y))$. The right route first applies $c_a$, then splits $b$ by $\sigma_X$, then applies the two $\kappa$ maps; it gives the identical last expression. Step 1 supplies precisely the normalized $c$ and $\sigma$ used here. Balancing and sheafification uniqueness as in Steps 2–3, and the direct-sum universal property in Step 4, extend this calculation to the stated equality of chain maps. Setting the suppressed scalar $a=1$ yields the abbreviated value in the statement. Step 5 retains every sequence transition.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: The unit maps have inverses $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. For $a=b$, $U_X$ sends $b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ to $ba\otimes x$, while $F_a(U_Y)$ sends its $\kappa^{aa}$ image to the same element. For $\sigma^{aa}$, applying $U_W$ in both tensor factors to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ gives $bx\otimes y$, the same as applying $U_W$ before the tensor comparison. Thus the identified maps are identities. The map $A_W$ is balanced: moving $r\in R_W^1$ from $d$ to $b$ replaces both expressions by $d i_W^{12}(r)i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x$; balancing over $R_W^0$ uses $i^{02}=i^{12}i^{01}$. Its inverse is $c\otimes x\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes x)$, and the composites are identities by balancing. These are sheaf and chain maps by the same universal property and degree-zero calculation already given.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Section 03EK tensor/bilinear universal property; agent calculation on the resulting normalized maps.

proof.text: For successive $\kappa$, start with $d\otimes(b\otimes(a\otimes x))$ in $S_X^{12}S_X^{01}F_0K$. The two successive comparisons, followed by $F_2(A_Y)$, give $d i_X^{12}(b)i_X^{02}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x)$ in $F_2S_Y^{02}K$. Applying $A_X$ first and then $\kappa^{02}$ gives the same value because $i_X^{02}=i_X^{12}i_X^{01}$. For successive $\sigma$, both routes on $d\otimes(b\otimes(x\otimes y))$, after the two target $A_W$ maps, give $(d i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, exactly as asserted. The sheafification and direct-sum uniqueness used above proves these identities on whole complexes, and Step 5 makes them strict-system equations. Finally each displayed route is an isomorphism in strict systems. If two composites are equal, multiplying by their inverses gives equality of the inverse composites; this proves every equation in the reverse direction as well. No part of these calculations used a nonzero element, division, flatness, or a bound on degrees.
